classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the central square and combine the two facing semicircles into one circular area before subtracting.

content.prompt: Find the area of the dark region to 2 d.p.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8 diagram below the prompt on the left.
spec.description: Two equal externally tangent circles, with horizontal segments joining their topmost and bottommost points. The upper and lower regions between their facing arcs have restrained blue shading. A vertical radius from the left circle's topmost point to its centre is labelled 4, with no printed unit.
spec.mathematics: Both radii are 4. The centres are 8 units apart. The central square has side 8, and its two excluded semicircles together have the area of one radius-4 circle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied radius label is visible; no calculated lengths, areas or solution annotations appear.

answer.worked:
The square has side length $2\times4=8$ units. The two semicircles within it have the area of one circle.

$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{square}} &= 8^2 \\
A_{\text{square}} &= 64 \\
A_{\text{circle}} &= \pi(4)^2 \\
A_{\text{circle}} &= 16\pi \\
A_{\text{dark}} &= 64-16\pi \\
A_{\text{dark}} &\approx 13.73\text{ units}^2
\end{align*}$$
